what_happened: The the person running Athena, relaying the owner's new focus (speed first, use GitHub runners for CI), re-ranked the queue by hand. They queued two new jobs (0rz6, shard CI tests across runners; anbv, use CI results instead of local checks). They parked the forecast idea as 8qds at low priority, with qkzw. They raised async jobs A4-A9 and the disk and check-speed fixes to urgent. They lowered three non-speed root-cause fixes to high. This was an intervention, not a job failure. The event lists no job, criteria, or checks.
cause: Athena has no place to record the owner's standing focus (such as "speed first") and no rule that turns it into item priorities. Priority is a per-item field set at queue time, so a change in focus means someone must find and edit every affected item. Ranking falls back to defaults, and the the person running Athena acts as the ranking brain. The owner's stated priority also sits only in conversation, so nothing checks that the queue order matches it.
prevention: Add an owner-focus record, a short ordered list of themes, each with a tag or keyword set, kept in the repo and changed only by the owner through a logged command. Queue ranking would derive each item's effective priority from the focus tags: items on the top theme rank urgent, off-theme root-cause items rank high, and parked ideas rank low. The plan and the drain would both read the derived priority. Changing the focus would re-rank the queue in one logged step. Athena would show the old and new order for the owner to confirm. Each item would also be tagged with a theme when it is queued.
proposed_request: Add an owner-focus setting that drives queue priority. (1) Store an ordered list of focus themes, each with a name and tags, in a records file that the records validation accepts. Add an `athena focus set` command that writes it and logs the change as an owner decision. (2) When an item is queued, Athena tags it with the matching theme from its request text. The queue computes each item's effective priority from its theme's rank: the top theme is urgent, other themes are high or normal, and items tagged `parked` are low. An explicit per-item priority set by the owner overrides the derived one. (3) The plan and the drain order by effective priority, then by age. (4) `athena focus set` prints the queue order before and after, and applies the change only on confirmation. (5) Acceptance: with themes [speed, correctness] and queued items tagged for each, changing the focus to put speed first reorders the queue with no per-item edits. Tests cover that case, an item with no matching theme, an owner override, and an empty focus list that leaves today's order unchanged. Tests also cover the replay of the existing queue, showing that the order is unchanged when no focus is set. Do not change CI sharding or the check-speed work, which are queued separately.
